$comment: Accepted, known-failing tests. Every entry here is a promise that someone looked at
this failure, understood it, and decided not to fix it yet - not that it was ignored.
The rule the runner enforces: a failure listed here reports as `info` with its age in
days; ANY failure not listed here is a blocker. That is the whole point. A suite with
standing red tests and no baseline teaches its owner to skim past red, and the fourth
failure - the real one - sails through. With a baseline, red means red again.
An entry that stops matching is reported as a stale waiver, because a baseline nobody
prunes slowly turns into a blindfold. Remove it when the test goes green.
Shape: { suite, file, test, reason, acceptedOn, owner }
Currently EMPTY, and that is the goal state. The three report-schedules waivers that
lived here were resolved on 2026-09-20 rather than carried: Ariel confirmed a reporting
period covers an Israeli calendar week or month, which made the code right and the
assertions stale, so the assertions were fixed. A waiver is a place to park a decision
nobody has made yet - not a place to keep one that has been made.
